CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect.

After his arrest, Anthony was charged with three felony counts of resisting an executive officer, one felony count of battery with injury on a peace officer, one misdemeanor count of exhibiting a concealable firearm in public, one misdemeanor count of having a concealed firearm, and one misdemeanor count of carrying a loaded firearm. The Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office listed Anthony as a serious danger to society, and he was court ordered to not possess any firearms, not leave the state of California, and attend at least three alcohol counseling meetings a week as conditions to his release. Anthony's attorney revealed in November of 2025 that he passed away in his parents' house in August, roughly six weeks after his arrest. According to reports, this was officially the first public mention of his passing. A handwritten note found in Isaiah's car that was initially believed to be a note was later determined to be a character witness statement for him from June of 2025, possibly due to his involvement with Adrian's arrest. An autopsy revealed Isaiah died from cocaine toxicity and found three plastic bindles typically used to hold drugs in his stomach. They ruled there was no foul play involved, citing no defensive wounds or signs of injury, concluding the death as an accidental overdose. Isaiah's family reportedly told courts he suffered from depression since being placed on administrative leave post arrest and struggled with cocaine and alcohol abuse in the past, but had been attending Alcoholics Anonymous, likely due to the court order. Had Isaiah been convicted of his charges, he would have faced up to seven years in state prison.
